headlines.headline: US index futures firmed slightly on Thanksgiving morning: Dow +0.6%, S&P 500 +0.8%, Nasdaq-100 +0.8% (IBD, latest read), vs +0.6%/+0.75%/+0.7% at 8 AM PT; cash markets closed for Thanksgiving, futures trade until 1 PM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is holding and inching higher into the holiday pause — but overnight futures on a closed market do not guarantee Friday's open, and Friday is a thin half session.

headlines.headline: South Korea's Fair Trade Commission moved to sanction Apple over iPhone 16 Apple Intelligence ads, saying features were advertised as available before they were — Siri personal-context support was pitched for Korean in early April 2025 but arrived only in October 2026, ~18 months late. Fine of up to 53.6B won (~$36M) proposed; Apple disputes the findings and has six weeks to respond. It would be the KFTC's first-ever fine on Apple, and follows a $250M US class-action settlement in May 2026 over the same delayed features.
headlines.why_it_matters: The fine itself is trivial against Apple's scale, but the delayed-AI-features issue is now a regulatory theme on two continents — a reputational drag on Apple's AI credibility just as it builds its own autonomous agent.

headlines.headline: A Maryland federal judge dismissed Amazon's challenge to CPSC recall orders covering 400,000+ hazardous Fulfilled-by-Amazon products (faulty carbon monoxide detectors, hair dryers lacking electrocution protection, children's sleepwear failing flammability standards), ruling Amazon is a distributor, not just a logistics provider, and must carry out the recalls — posting notices, emailing buyers and refunding on proof of destruction.
headlines.why_it_matters: A legal precedent that raises Amazon's product-safety compliance burden for third-party goods, but the direct cost looks modest and the stock impact is likely limited — a headline risk, not an earnings event.

headlines.headline: Markets price a December Fed rate hike at 97.9% likelihood, per LSEG, after hot October core PCE; the 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.845% (Wednesday's close, -6bp) with futures implying ~+2bp.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hike is now near-fully priced, so the December 8-9 meeting is about the path after, not the decision — any dovish surprise in the statement or presser would matter more than the hike itself.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news overnight. Carry-forward: a Nov 24 Zacks piece frames the growth case — $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted, record $23.14/month revenue per horsepower (+8% y/y), with LNG exports and power demand seen needing 10M+ additional compression horsepower; Zacks raised FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24), FY2027 at $1.31, and holds a Hold rating; a Nov 26 Seeking Alpha note also rates USAC a Hold — 8.88% yield covered, but limited upside at 8.29x forward EV/EBITDA amid substantial debt — countering the Nov 25 buy-rated piece at $23.63 citing the 8.9% yield, 1.67x distribution coverage and record pricing. USAC opened Wednesday at $23.04. Q3 2026 (Nov 3): revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
